answer.policy_title: CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion Guidelines (part of eviCore's Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines)
criteria_quotes: The determination of medical necessity for the performance of anterior cervical fusion with discectomy/corpectomy (with or without osteotomy) is always made on a case-by-case basis.

Initial primary anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met: Radiculopathy ... Myelopathy ...

Radiculopathy - Subjective symptoms include BOTH of the following: Significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.); Unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Objective physical exam findings include ANY of the following: Dermatomal sensory deficit; Motor deficit (e.g., biceps, triceps weakness); Reflex changes; Shoulder abduction relief sign; Nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver)

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): Prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for 6 weeks; Provider-directed exercise program ... for 6 weeks; Epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery

MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following: Herniated disc(s) ...; Synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst; Central/lateral/foraminal stenosis; Osteophytes

Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following: Individual is a never-smoker; Individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least 6 weeks prior to planned surgery as evidenced by blood cotinine lab results of ≤10 ng/mL

Myelopathy - Subjective symptoms include ANY of the following: Upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; Fine motor dysfunction...; Gait disturbance; New-onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; Frequent falls ... MRI/CT shows findings that are concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that are caused by EITHER of the following: Cervical spinal cord compression; Cervical spinal stenosis
Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-08-19), i.e., must be received by 2027-02-15, as stated in the denial letter.
answer.submission_route: Mail the completed Complaint and Appeal form to: Moda Health, Attn: Appeal unit, P.O. Box 40384, Portland, OR 97240. Alternatively, fax to 503-412-4003 or 866-923-0412. Questions can be directed to Moda Health Customer Service at 855-294-1668 (or the member-services number on the back of the ID card). The member/provider should use Moda Health's 'Complaint and appeal form' (available at modahealth.com/pdfs/grievance_form.pdf) and attach supporting medical records, imaging, and a letter addressing each unmet criterion.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Moda Health's own current provider authorization page states that authorizations for 'advanced imaging and musculoskeletal services' — the category that includes spine surgery procedures such as CPT 22551 — 'are obtained through EviCore,' a Moda Health partner, and that clinicians should consult EviCore's Provider Portal (www.evicore.com) for the applicable clinical guidelines. EviCore publishes its Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines, of which CMM-601 (Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion) is the document specifically addressing CPT 22551. This is the document located and quoted above. answer.notes: Moda Health does not appear to publish its own standalone 'cervical fusion' medical necessity criteria document on modahealth.com (older URLs like CervicalFusion.pdf and LumbarFusion.pdf now 404). Instead, Moda's current provider-facing materials (its Idaho/Alaska authorizations page and a Moda-specific eviCore FAQ titled 'Pain Management, Spine and Joint Surgery') confirm that Moda delegates prior-authorization medical necessity review for spine surgery (including ACDF, CPT 22551) to eviCore healthcare. EviCore's publicly posted clinical guideline 'CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion Guidelines,' effective November 1, 2024 (Version 2.0.2024), is the specific criteria document covering this exact procedure/CPT code. This is the most likely governing document, but because the denial letter itself does not cite a policy name or number, this identification is based on Moda's delegation structure rather than an explicit citation in the notice.
